source: Consent is genuine only if it is informed. This consent is not informed. Therefore this consent is not genuine.

reconstruction.title: Argument about the genuineness of consent

claims.text: Consent is genuine only if it is informed.

evidence.quote: Consent is genuine only if it is informed.

claims.text: Therefore this consent is not genuine.

evidence.quote: Therefore this consent is not genuine.

formalization.domain_description: The domain consists of all consents. The constant 'c' refers to the specific consent under discussion.

symbols.name: Genuine
symbols.meaning: Genuine(x) is true when consent x is genuine

symbols.name: Informed
symbols.meaning: Informed(x) is true when consent x is informed

translations.reason: Translates 'Consent is genuine only if it is informed' as a universal conditional statement
Translates 'This consent is not informed' using the constant c for the specific consent
Translates 'This consent is not genuine' using the constant c for the specific consent

interpretation_notes: The universal quantifier in c1 captures the general principle about all consents
The constant 'c' represents the specific consent mentioned in premises c2 and conclusion c3
The argument structure follows modus tollens: from (P→Q) and ¬Q, infer ¬P applied to the specific consent c
